name: Dreams Sapphire Resort & Spa

kids_club.evidence: Explorer's Club (3-12) is included, open 9am-10pm, with its own small pool, splash park and toddler pool added in the 2021 conversion; 2026 reviews are consistently positive about the kids' activities.

water_play.evidence: Family water park with three slides, a splash pad and a children's wading pool, alongside the main pool.

beach.evidence: Long white-sand beach behind the reef with a built breakwater that keeps swimming calm; reviews still note seasonal seaweed in the water.

rooms.evidence: Entry Junior Suites (about 520 sq ft) come with two double beds, and two-bedroom Family Suites were added in the 2021 conversion; connecting options are mentioned by one guide.

food.evidence: Six à la carte venues (grill, Italian/Mediterranean, Mexican, teppanyaki, adults-only French, plus a lunch grill) and a buffet, mostly without reservations; teppanyaki seats are forfeited if late, and quality varies.

condition.evidence: Converted from Now Sapphire in late 2021 with a new water park and room categories, with further work around 2024 and a newer Club & Villas section; standard areas still look older in places.

kids_club.name: Explorer's Club
kids_club.notes: Has its own small pool, splash park and toddler pool; beach campouts and crafts. Core Zone teen club also on site.

pros: Water park with three slides and a splash pad
Kids' club open 9am-10pm, with its own pool
Breakwater keeps the swimming area calm for young children
Junior Suites with two double beds, plus two-bedroom Family Suites
cons: Seaweed still reaches the beach in season
Standard rooms and some common areas are older and less cool than the newer Club section
Collared-shirt dress code at most dinner restaurants
Large resort (over 500 suites), so walks are long
verdict: The best all-round fit of these five for young children: a strong kids' club, a real water park and a calm breakwater beach, close to the airport.
